pr_title: sd: Return ret if error in sdmmc_spi_read_cxd
pr_body: - Add return ret if CMD fails in spi_read
pr_comments:
> Does this fix the issue described in #55769 on your board?

Kind of, it returns back to the inital init function with the -ENOTSUP as it should, but the CS pin is never released, causing problems other places, so there is more going on here.

It didn't release the CS pin before this PR either, to be fair. but it did before the changes in https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/b7cd970493659848d407cc5a8792079408791ea2

I added a check of the OCR that is read by using CMD58. If OCR == 0 we should reject the card as no operating conditions are set. I have verified that this fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/55769 and have also verified that with an SD card inserted it passes and works as normal.
@danieldegrasse @jfischer-no
@danieldegrasse or @jfischer-no: Do you see any issues with checking the OCR value and rejecting the card if no values are set?

> @danieldegrasse or @jfischer-no: Do you see any issues with checking the OCR value and rejecting the card if no values are set?

It should be ok to do this- the OCR value should always have some voltage range value set. I've tested this PR on a K64F and it functions correctly.

issue_context.title: samples/subsys/fs/fat_fs: Infinite loop if SD card is not inserted
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
If you run the above sample without an SD card inserted, the code will not return an appropriate error, but hang in an infinite loop.
Output: 
```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.2.0-5640-g33220ef086cc ***
[00:00:00.258,697] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.259,429] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.260,162] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.260,864] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.261,596] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.262,329] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.263,031] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.263,763] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.264,495] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.265,197] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.265,930] <inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support
[00:00:00.265,930] <inf> sd: Card does not support CMD8, assuming legacy card
```

This was tested using latest main (33220ef086cc13e9f0e2334fbe4a853876792414) and the target `nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp `.
This worked in November, so I will start a bisect now to find what changes have happened.


**Expected behavior**
A proper error return code from `disk_access_init(...)` if the SD card is not present.

**Impact**
Unsure yet, but may be severe if this hangs for all DKs with no SD card inserted.
comments: Bisect completed. The change which causes this comes from https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/b7cd970493659848d407cc5a8792079408791ea2

@koffes Appreciate you bisecting this- I don't have a Nordic board to reproduce on, but I cannot reproduce this using a FRDM-K64F, which uses the same SPI based SDHC driver that the `nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp` does.

I see the following output when running `samples/subsys/fs/fatfs` without an SD card inserted:

```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.3.0-1109-g33220ef086cc ***
[00:00:00.004,000] <err> sd: Card error on CMD0
[00:00:00.004,000] <err> main: Storage init ERROR!
[00:00:00.009,000] <err> sd: Card error on CMD0
[00:00:00.009,000] <err> fs: fs mount error (-5)
Error mounting disk.
```

Can you see where the code hangs on your board? I would expect CMD0 to return an error when no card is inserted.
Thanks for the reply, We will have a look and get back to you.

I can reproduce it on nrf5340_audio_dk_nrf5340_cpuapp, seems to be board specific.
Using nRF5340dk and a shield with SD card slot (e.g. waveshare_epaper_gdeh0154a07) it works as expected:

```
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.3.0-1346-g4408c058789e ***
[00:00:00.258,911] <err> sd: Card error on CMD0
[00:00:00.258,941] <err> main: Storage init ERROR!
[00:00:00.264,129] <err> sd: Card error on CMD0
[00:00:00.264,129] <err> fs: fs mount error (-5)
Error mounting disk.
```

I've done some digging/debugging and can see that we get:
`<inf> sd: Legacy card detected, no CMD8 support, resp: 0x0000`
11 times, since the number of retries is set to 10, then we get:
`<inf> sd: Card does not support CMD8, assuming legacy card`
after which it calls 'sd_idle(card)'. This returns 0 to sd_command_init() which then continues with 
```C
if (!sdmmc_card_init(card)) {
	return 0;
}
```

Is this right? I would assume that if the response in sd_send_interface_condition is 0x0000 then it means there is no card present? Or is the problem that 
```C
sdhc_request(card->sdhc, &cmd, NULL);
```
should have returned an error?
The SPI bus (spi4 node) is shared between sdhc0 and cs47l63 (IMO design issue), I suggest to look there at line states/configuration.
Forgot to mention that this is when there is no SD card inserted, of course. When the SD card is inserted, everything works as normal.

> Is this right? I would assume that if the response in sd_send_interface_condition is 0x0000 then it means there is no card present? Or is the problem that
>
> ```
> sdhc_request(card->sdhc, &cmd, NULL);
> ```
>
> should have returned an error?

`sdhc_request` should indeed return an error on CMD0 when no card is inserted. 

> The SPI bus (spi4 node) is shared between sdhc0 and cs47l63 (IMO design issue), I suggest to look there at line states/configuration.

This is where I would look as well. I wonder if the other device on the bus is causing the data read during `sdhc_request` to match what would be expected from an SD card as a response to CMD0, resulting in `sdhc_request` succeeding when it should not

I've looked at the SPI lines and here you can see how it looked like before the changes in the upmerge:
![SD_Card_before_upmerge](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36298637/226283445-3e600156-4a6d-4bb4-a705-ee8e20ee2d1c.png)
and this is after the changes in the upmerge:
![SD_Card_after_upmerge](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/36298637/226283504-64d35f95-92f5-404a-ba33-1ac7d821bdce.png)
As you can see, there is nothing on the MISO, and the CS for CS47L63 stays high. I also see that there are more calls to the SPI. I've added the capture here as well:
[After upmerge with SD.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/11015600/After.upmerge.with.SD.zip)

I see that we never got an error on CMD0, this is what catched our card not being present previously:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/b7cd970493659848d407cc5a8792079408791ea2#diff-4a67a43d4bc3538adb35bf77e1ed507aad8c5ae4584f85c7bfb5e4b2b2eace5aL195

We have done some more debugging and see that sdhc_request expects the MISO to be high if no SD card present. Since we have a level shifter in our design and the pin is floating when there is no SD card, it seems the level shifter is pulling the MISO low when CS is low. If the SD card spec says MISO has to be high when no card is present that is something we have to fix for the next spin of our board. 

This is however not going to fix the problem for all of our current boards. Is there a place where the spec expects something else than 0 as a response that could be checked? [Here](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/837091c05627950adfbd8bc47fe57560ec39607d/subsys/sd/sdmmc.c#L556) for instance?
@koffes Are you ok if I close this issue? It seems like the problem has been resolved using the additional check in the SD stack.

review_comments: I see that from before, this ret value was not checked.
